schema.browserReq: A browser with WebCodecs (recent Chrome or Edge, Safari 16.4+)
schema.description: A video editor that runs entirely in the browser: cut on a timeline, grade with curves and .cube LUTs, key a green screen, keyframe and track masks, and transcribe captions locally. Exports MP4 in 16:9, 9:16, 1:1 and 4:5 up to 4K in H.264, HEVC or AV1, or MP3. Free, no watermark, nothing is ever uploaded.

hero.title:
Edited here.
Seen everywhere.
hero.lead: A complete video editor that runs on your own computer or phone: timeline, captions, grading, tracked masks, export up to 4K. Your footage is never uploaded.
hero.note: Free · No account · Nothing to install
cut.title: A real timeline. The shortcuts you already know.
cut.lead: Stack video, b-roll and music. Split a clip with <kbd>S</kbd>, drag its edges, move it to another track.
cut.p1.title: Split, trim, nudge
cut.p1.body: <kbd>S</kbd> splits under the playhead, the edges drag, <kbd>N</kbd> turns snapping on and off.
cut.p2.title: As many tracks as the edit needs
cut.p2.body: Video, b-roll, titles and music, each on its own track. Drag a clip from one to another.
cut.p3.title: Thumb or keyboard
cut.p3.body: On a phone, CapCut's gestures. At a desk, the shortcuts of Vegas and Premiere.
captions.title: Captions, transcribed on your own machine.
captions.lead: Start the transcription: it runs on your own machine, and every line lands on the timeline as a text clip you can correct, move and restyle. An SRT, VTT or ASS file you already have imports the same way.
captions.cue.1: Right, let's take it from the top.
captions.cue.3: And the titles come in here.
captions.note: Transcription needs a device with enough power, and SelfCut checks before offering it. The speech model downloads once and is cached afterwards; your audio never leaves the browser.
formats.title: One edit, every format.
formats.lead: Say where the video is going. SelfCut handles the framing, the resolution and the file.
formats.169: MP4, up to 4K · keeps your footage's frame rate
formats.916: MP4, up to 4K · full frame, no letterbox
formats.mp3: Keep the sound, drop the picture
formats.more: Also: Instagram 1:1 and 4:5 · H.264, HEVC or AV1 · 720p to 4K · a 120 fps cadence · 24p cinema · a light file for email.
defaults.title: Right for the platform before you touch a setting
defaults.loud.dd: The mix is brought to -14 LUFS with a limiter at -1 dB, the level YouTube and TikTok play without turning it down.
defaults.frame.dd: Follows your footage, up to 120 fps.
defaults.fill.dd: Vertical fills the whole frame, with no black bars.
defaults.files.dd: A standard MP4 or MP3, no watermark, ready to post or to hand to an editor.
depth.title: When the edit asks for more.
depth.lead: None of this is on screen until you go looking for it. It is there when a cut needs more than a cut.
depth.grade.dd: Brightness, contrast, saturation, white balance, tint, vignette, blur and sharpening; per-channel tone curves; .cube LUTs imported once and reused across clips; chroma key for a green screen. Every one of them also runs on a mask, so a grade can land on a face or a sky rather than the whole frame. Waveform, RGB parade, histogram and vectorscope to check the result.
depth.keyframes.dd: Position, scale, stretch, rotation, opacity and every colour parameter, with easing presets or per-segment Bézier handles, edited on property lanes under the clip.
depth.masks.dd: Rectangle, ellipse or a Bézier pen-tool shape, feathered and invertible. A motion tracker makes one follow a face, a plate or a screen, which you then blur or pixelate in place.
depth.text.dd: Titles with six faces, an outline and a caption pill, solid colours, gradients and drawn shapes. Nine transitions rendered from the overlap between two clips.
proof.title: Your footage stays on your machine.
proof.1.title: Footage that cannot leave this room
proof.1.body: Rushes under NDA, minors' faces, a medical or legal file, a journalist's source. Everything happens on your machine: there is no server to send anything to.
proof.2.title: Nothing to install, nothing to pay
proof.2.body: One tab. No account, no watermark, no pro tier waiting for you.
proof.3.title: Your machine encodes, so there is no queue
proof.3.body: No export quota, no render waiting behind everyone else's. A faster computer means a faster export.
proof.lead: SelfCut decodes, edits and encodes inside your browser. There is no server to send anything to, no account to create, no queue to wait in.
spec.title: And the rest of it
spec.sound.dd: Volume, pan, speed, fades, volume envelopes, and audio effects: leveler, voice, bass, reverb, echo.
spec.import.dd: MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV, MP3, WAV, FLAC, images and SRT/VTT/ASS. An audio track the browser can't play is converted, not dropped.
spec.preview.dd: Picture and sound stay in sync as you scrub.
spec.lang.dd: English, French, Spanish, German, Portuguese (Brazil), Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Korean.
spec.resume.dt: Picks up where you left off
spec.resume.dd: Projects save themselves, on your device.
faq.title: Common questions
faq.q1: Are my videos uploaded to a server?
faq.a1: No. Editing happens in your browser, on your device. Your videos go nowhere: nobody else can see them, us included.
faq.a2: Yes, entirely. Editing runs on your device, so there are no servers to pay for, and nothing to bill you for.
faq.a3: MP4 in 16:9 for YouTube, MP4 in 9:16 for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, and MP3 if you only want the sound.
faq.q4: Does SelfCut work on a phone?
faq.a4: Yes. On a phone you edit with touch gestures, like CapCut. On a computer you get a precise timeline and the keyboard shortcuts of Premiere or Vegas.
faq.q5: Which browsers does SelfCut work in?
faq.a5: A recent Chrome, Edge, or Safari 16.4+. SelfCut decodes and encodes video on your own device through the WebCodecs API, and a browser that does not expose it gets a short explanation screen instead of a broken editor.
faq.q6: Are my projects saved, and can I move one to another computer?
faq.a6: Yes, automatically, in the browser on your device: reopen SelfCut and your edit is where you left it. One caveat: clearing the site's data clears the project with it. To put an edit somewhere safe, or carry it to another machine, save a .selfcut file. It holds the timeline and the asset details, not the video itself, which keeps it small; SelfCut asks you to reconnect the source files when you reopen it, matching them back by name, so pointing it at the folder is enough.
